event: Elsie puts on her cleanest halter, pins her clip twice over, and waters the plants.
Tamsin comes to the bakery door with her hair wet and combed flat, which it never is.
Elsie says she looks lovely; Tamsin says she looks like a drowned cat, and goes red.
Through the Tether Elsie feels something tight and cold in Tamsin, like a held breath.
Tamsin carries the cake as if it might go off, and they set out along Thimble Canal.
Elsie buys a bunch of marigolds at a flower stall for Tamsin's mother, and pays for them.
Tamsin stares at the marigolds and laughs once, oddly.
She walks slower with every bridge they cross.
Elsie asks if her mother is frightening; Tamsin says she is the kindest woman alive.
Tamsin says she hasn't been home in a year; Elsie asks why, and Tamsin keeps walking.
The Long Cut coal wharf is a stone quay heaped with coal, barges moored nose to tail.
Tamsin stops at the head of the quay, and stays there.
She points down the line at a long green barge with geraniums all along its cabin roof.
She says it's the Marigold, and Elsie looks down at her flowers and laughs.
Tamsin says she can't, says it twice, and her hands shake round the cake.
Elsie takes the cake from her, then takes her hand, and keeps it.
She says they can stand here as long as Tamsin likes, and they stand.
A girl with copper curls tied up in blue cloth jumps off the Marigold with a rope.
She sees Tamsin, drops the rope, and runs the length of the quay.
Tamsin steps back; the girl throws both arms round her anyway and holds on.
The girl is Nell, Tamsin's little sister, and she is crying and laughing at once.
Elsie sees a thin pale scar across the back of Nell's left hand, on Tamsin's shoulder.
Something in Tamsin cracks wide down the Tether, and Elsie feels it in her own chest.
A broad woman with greying curls climbs out of the cabin and shouts Tamsin's name.
Rosa Reyes comes at a run in her coal-dusted apron and wraps both her girls up at once.
Tamsin stands stiff in the middle of them, and then all at once she softens.
Rosa holds Tamsin's face in both hands, says she's too thin, and says come aboard.
Rosa turns to Elsie; Tamsin says this is Elsie, and can't seem to say more.
Elsie gives Rosa the marigolds and the honey cake, and says she helped bake it last night.
Rosa smells the paper and says that is Agnes Merriweather's cake or she's a heron.
Elsie says Agnes taught her; Rosa says Agnes never taught anyone, and looks at Elsie hard.
The Marigold's cabin is low and snug, with a black stove, bright cups and geraniums at the glass.
Rosa makes tea and cuts the cake, and eats the first slice with her eyes shut.
She says it tastes just as it did at her own wedding, and wipes her eyes on her shawl.
Nell sits pressed against Tamsin on the bench, and Tamsin keeps her hands under the table.
Elsie notices Tamsin watching Nell's left hand every time it moves.
Rosa asks Elsie what class she drew; Elsie says Enthraller, and the cabin goes quiet.
Rosa looks at Tamsin; Tamsin says Elsie is the one who reached her in the red.
Tamsin says she slept the night through after, for the first time in a year.
Rosa puts down her cup and asks Elsie if that's true.
Elsie says yes, and that Tamsin can break the Tether whenever she likes.
Rosa reaches across the table and takes Elsie's hand in both of hers, coal dust and all.
Nell asks Elsie to help with the geraniums, and takes her up onto the cabin roof.
Nell pinches dead heads off the geraniums and asks how Tamsin really is.
Elsie tells her honestly: brave, loud, and ashamed of something she won't say.
Nell holds up her scarred hand and says that's the something.
She says Tamsin's first red took her at her own Naming, and Nell was standing nearest.
Nell says she never once blamed her, but Tamsin ran anyway, and never came home.
Nell says she writes Tamsin a letter every week and sends none, and laughs at herself.
Elsie's eyes fill; she says Tamsin should hear all that from Nell herself.
Nell looks at her a long moment, then hugs her hard round the neck.
Elsie hugs her back, and Nell grins exactly the way Tamsin does.
Down in the cabin Tamsin sits on a narrow bunk made up neat under a patched quilt.
Rosa says it's Tamsin's, and she has made it up fresh every week of the year.
Tamsin puts her face in her hands, and Rosa sits beside her and rubs slow circles on her back.
Elsie feels the ache come down the Tether, and sits on Tamsin's other side.
Nell comes down with a fat bundle of letters tied in string, and sets it on Tamsin's knees.
Tamsin unties it and reads the top one, with Elsie leaning on her shoulder.
It is about a heron that stole Nell's lunch, and it ends: come home, I'm not cross.
Tamsin laughs and cries at once, and takes Nell's scarred hand in hers and holds it.
Rosa says they load coal till noon, and hands everyone aboard a job.
Tamsin carries sacks aboard two at a time; Elsie and Nell sweep the quay and sing.
Elsie hums a caravan song, and Rosa knows the words and sings them louder.
Coal dust smudges Elsie's cheek, and Tamsin wipes it off with her thumb and goes red.
They eat bread and pickled eggs on deck in the sun, and Rosa feeds everyone twice.
Rosa asks about Elsie's mother, and Elsie tells her about the caravan roads.
Elsie says she writes her mother every week; Nell says at least Elsie posts hers.
In the afternoon Tamsin walks Elsie to the end of the wharf, by the lock's black gates.
Tamsin says she broke the Hounds' shield-bearer's arm, but Nell's hand was the first.
She says she was sure she would hurt Elsie in the Glasswood, until the thread came.
Elsie says she wasn't afraid of her for a moment, and Tamsin hears that she means it.
Tamsin leans her forehead on Elsie's with her eyes shut, so close their breath mixes.
Elsie says she loves her, and Tamsin makes a sound as if she's been punched.
A barge horn blows at the lock, and Tamsin straightens and says they should go back.
Rosa cooks fish stew in one pot for the four of them, and won't hear of anyone leaving.
She says the Marigold stays tied up till the day after tomorrow, so tonight they both sleep aboard.
Tamsin starts to say Elsie has her own room; Elsie says yes please before she finishes.
Rosa plays her squeezebox on deck under the canal lanterns, and Nell makes Elsie dance.
Tamsin watches from the cabin roof, and doesn't dance, and doesn't look away.
There are three bunks for four of them, so Elsie and Tamsin share Tamsin's narrow one.
Tamsin lies on the very edge; Elsie pulls her in by the arm so she won't fall out.
Elsie falls asleep at once, her face in Tamsin's neck and a hand on her shirt.
Elsie half-wakes to Tamsin's heart racing under her palm, and thinks it a bad dream.
She murmurs that it's all right and holds her tighter, and Tamsin's breath stops.
Something warm and huge comes down the Tether, and Tamsin's hand comes up to rest on Elsie's hair.
